events.content:
UserDashboard in app/UserDashboard.tsx is now an async server component. It fetches https://api.example.com/user/preferences with cache: 'no-store', so the data is fetched fresh on every request.

It follows the same pattern as app/page.tsx: a helper function does the fetch inside a try/catch, returns mock data if the call fails (for example at build time), and the component awaits it. The helper also treats a non-OK HTTP status as a failure. The component shows each preference as a key: value list item. page.tsx needed no changes because it already renders <UserDashboard />.

Checks:
- npx tsc --noEmit -p . passed (exit 0).
- npm run build succeeded, and the / route is now listed as ƒ (Dynamic), meaning it renders on each request instead of being built as a static page.

The real API wasn't called: api.example.com is a placeholder address, so running this won't show real data.

The build also added .next/dev/types//.ts to the include list in your tsconfig.json. Next.js does this automatically; I left it in place.
